clue.text: Particularly large vehicles, a lot of which 12 collected

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
cars are vehicles

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a fleet of oversized vehicles, many of which a collector gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: The film of My Fair Lady (12) won eight Academy Awards, so 'a lot of which 12 collected' defines the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The film My Fair Lady won eight Academy Awards, the statuettes being a lot of what it collected.

clue.text: Among Irish, a writer

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the run of words Irish, a writer

explanation.surface: Picking out a writer from among the Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the playwright was himself an Irish writer, and he hides across 'Irish, a w'.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish-born playwright and critic, so he is a writer among the Irish.

clue.text: A top detective's gathered together drug addicts

parts.note: a top detective is the head of the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: A senior police officer has rounded up a group of junkies.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police's Criminal Investigation Department; 'gathered together' just joins the pieces, and the surface's police raid is a natural home for addicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidhead is slang for a habitual user of the hallucinogen LSD, a kind of drug addict.

clue.text: Smoothly finished a little after second

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the abbreviation for second

parts.note: little means tiny

explanation.surface: Something was completed a moment after the second hand ticked.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiny describes a surface with the smooth glossy finish of satin cloth.

clue.text: Creator's drive reduced by 50%?

parts.note: demi is the prefix meaning half
an urge is an inner drive

explanation.surface: A question whether a maker's ambition has been halved.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'drive reduced by 50%' as half-urge; the 's after Creator stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Platonic philosophy the demiurge is the divine craftsman who fashions the world, a creator.

clue.text: Sound like 21, initially, and lack aspiration?

definitions.meaning: Eliza Doolittle (21) begins the play speaking Cockney, leaving the h off words such as 'ow' and 'appy'
aspiration is the breathy h sound, so to lack it is to leave that sound out; the question mark flags the pun on ambition

explanation.surface: Advice to talk like Eliza at first and give up ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: An aitch is the letter H; dropping it is a hallmark of London Cockney speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping your aitches means omitting the h sound, the breathy aspiration, as Cockney speakers like the early Eliza do.

clue.text: Gradually become colour seen in cut fruit

indicators.note: seen in places the colour inside the shortened fruit
cut means the fruit loses its last letter

parts.note: a melon is a fruit
a tint is a colour

explanation.surface: A shade of colour is visible inside a sliced piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like sliced fruit in the surface, but it signals dropping the fruit's last letter; 'seen in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To melt into something is to merge with it by degrees, gradually becoming it.

clue.text: Strip off gear, appearing in Sun, right?

indicators.note: appearing in says the letters are to be found within the words Sun, right

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a gear-stripping story ran in a tabloid paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, which makes 'appearing in' look like publication.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig a ship is to strip off its rigging, the gear of ropes and sails.

clue.text: Environmental group wants space for putting energy in measure

parts.note: a golf green is the area where players putt

indicators.note: in places the energy symbol inside the measure

parts.note: a pace is a measure of length
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone needs room to fit an energy-saving scheme into a policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' suggests placing, but here it is the golf stroke on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenpeace is an international environmental campaigning organisation.

clue.text: Do air broadcast by centre of network, part of BBC

indicators.note: by places the network's centre beside the anagram
broadcast means the letters of do air are scattered and rearranged
centre of picks the middle letters of network

explanation.surface: An instruction to do some airtime on a national broadcasting network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges DO AIR to RADIO; the centre of neTWOrk is TWO.
explanation.definitionFit: BBC Radio 2 is one of the British Broadcasting Corporation's national radio stations.

clue.text: Writer of 12, sounds like a beginner

indicators.note: sounds like says the word for a beginner is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a beginner is a learner

explanation.surface: The author of a famous musical is said to be a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Jay Lerner wrote the book and lyrics of the musical My Fair Lady (12).

clue.text: Professor initially appearing twice in a row in this puzzle

definitions.text: Professor initially appearing twice in a row in this puzzle

parts.words: Professor initially appearing twice in a row in this puzzle
parts.note: the professor of the theme play has both names starting with H, so his initial appears twice, and he sits in an across row of this grid

explanation.surface: A professor whose initial letter turns up twice running in this crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a row' means both the two Hs side by side as initials and an across entry, which this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Professor Higgins is the phonetics teacher in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, initials H.H.

clue.text: Person told about Thames disaster in movie

definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme London Bridge Is Falling Down addresses each verse's news of the collapsing bridge to a lady so named
the 1964 film musical of Shaw's Pygmalion

explanation.surface: Someone informed of a calamity on the river appears in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs 'London Bridge is falling down, falling down, falling down, London Bridge is falling down, my fair lady', the Thames disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The film musical based on Pygmalion is titled with the words that end each verse of London Bridge Is Falling Down.

clue.text: Unknown taken in by eccentric man that can be taught to speak

definitions.text: that can be taught to speak
definitions.note: a relative phrase standing for the noun it describes, a bird that mimics speech

indicators.note: taken in by puts the unknown inside the rearranged letters
eccentric means the letters of man are put in an odd order

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An odd man takes in an unknown, a bird that can learn to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges MAN to MNA, and 'taken in by' puts Y inside it after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a starling-family bird famous for imitating human speech.

clue.text: Middle of tune recorded without piano, yet to be used

indicators.note: Middle of picks the central letters of tune
without in its old sense of outside: the recording wraps round the piano

parts.note: taped means recorded
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: The core of a melody was recorded without a piano and has never been used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside: TAPED goes round P.
explanation.definitionFit: An untapped resource has not yet been drawn on, so it is still to be used.

clue.text: Colonel dramatically choosing to protect king

indicators.note: to protect means the choosing word surrounds the king like a guard

parts.note: picking means choosing
ER is Edwardus Rex, the cipher of King Edward

explanation.surface: An officer chooses, in a theatrical way, to guard the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dramatically' marks a character in a play: Colonel Pickering is Higgins's friend in Pygmalion.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Pickering is the phonetics enthusiast who bets with Higgins in Pygmalion and My Fair Lady.

clue.text: Witticisms about girl 2 wrote three dramas for

indicators.note: about means the witticisms go round the girl

parts.note: puns are witticisms
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Jokes about a girl for whom a playwright wrote three plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw (2) published 'Three Plays for Puritans' in 1901.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's 1901 collection was titled Three Plays for Puritans, naming the readers he wrote them for.

clue.text: Instrument showing fish in front of area round boat

indicators.note: in front of puts the fish before the following pieces

parts.note: a bass is a fish
a tub is a slang word for a slow boat

explanation.surface: A fish is shown ahead of an area surrounding a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass tuba is the lowest-pitched brass instrument in the tuba family.

clue.text: Form of address for East Enders? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half the word survives, losing its second half

parts.note: Cockneys are natives of the East End of London

explanation.surface: A question about how people in London's East End address each other, answered emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is also British slang for 'very much so', which disguises the instruction to halve COCKNEYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock is an informal Cockney form of address between men, like 'mate'.

clue.text: Player of 21, originally, almost a saint

indicators.note: almost means the actress's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Julie Andrews created the role of Eliza (21) on Broadway in 1956

explanation.surface: An actor from the original cast nearly reaches sainthood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' refers to the first stage production; Audrey Hepburn played Eliza in the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew the Apostle is a saint, patron saint of Scotland.

clue.text: In earlier life, former partner one's caught in act

indicators.note: caught in means the former partner and one's are trapped inside the act

parts.note: a pretence is an act
an ex is a former partner
one's is I'S, I being the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: In a previous life, an ex was caught putting on an act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; 'caught in' puts EXIS inside PRETENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-existence is the idea of a soul's life before its present incarnation, an earlier life.

clue.text: Dramatic heroine is final character included by essayist

indicators.note: included by means the final character sits inside the essayist's pen name

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb
Z is the final character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A stage heroine is the last character an essayist wrote in.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza Doolittle is the flower-girl heroine of Pygmalion and My Fair Lady.

clue.text: Charity making Doolittle lose heart

indicators.note: lose heart means the central letters of the name are taken out

explanation.surface: A charity makes Eliza's father despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose heart' strips OLITT from the middle of DOOLITTLE, leaving the two letters at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: Dole in its older sense is a charitable gift of food or money handed out to the poor.

clue.text: Snobbish boy and girl

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A snooty boy and girl.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da means pretentiously refined in speech or manner, affectedly posh.

clue.text: Player selected for part of 11, one of famous group

definitions.meaning: Cast as Professor Higgins (11) in the stage and film musical
George ... was one of the Beatles

explanation.surface: An actor chosen for a role, and a member of a well-known band.
explanation.definitionFit: Rex Harrison played Higgins on stage and screen, and George Harrison played guitar in the Beatles.

clue.text: Gets around through use of quiet donkeys

parts.note: by means through the use of, as in 'by hand'
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
asses are donkeys

explanation.surface: Someone travels about quietly on donkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to go round it rather than through, to get around it.

clue.text: Ring producer 2 criticised early in his career

definitions.meaning: the composer who created the opera cycle The Ring of the Nibelung
Shaw (2) began as a London music critic and wrote The Perfect Wagnerite about this composer

explanation.surface: A maker of rings was reviewed by a playwright when young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring producer' suggests a jeweller; it is the composer of the four-opera Ring cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner composed Der Ring des Nibelungen, and Shaw reviewed his music as a young critic.
